before: To connect scattered personal wrong-question records with analysis and follow-up practice, this project designs and implements an AI-powered wrong-question analysis and learning recommendation system based on the Zhipu GLM model. The system uses Vue 3, TypeScript, Spring Boot, MyBatis-Plus and MySQL in a decoupled front-end and back-end architecture. Retrieval from the learner's own question collection supplies model context, while the platform validates and stores analyses and variant exercises. Functions include question recording, image-assisted input, similar-question retrieval, practice records, fixed-schedule review and learning reports. Role and ownership checks constrain data access. Evaluation includes offline automated tests, integration with an isolated database, live model calls and controlled small-sample experiments. The results support functional operation under the tested conditions, without establishing general educational effectiveness. Question-level status uses a rule-based score rather than probabilistic knowledge tracing. The system implements personal knowledge-content caching, unpractised-question selection and generation after resource exhaustion, with claims limited to the verified scope.
after: To connect scattered personal wrong-question records with analysis and follow-up practice, this project designs and implements an AI-powered wrong-question analysis and learning recommendation system based on the Zhipu GLM model. The system uses Vue 3, TypeScript, Spring Boot, MyBatis-Plus and MySQL in a decoupled front-end and back-end architecture. Retrieval from the learner's own question collection supplies model context, and the platform validates and stores auxiliary analyses and practice resources. It reuses valid knowledge content and unpractised questions before generating additional resources, while recording actual attempts, fixed-schedule reviews and rule-based question scores. Students, teachers and administrators access functions according to their roles and data ownership. Engineering tests, previously recorded live model calls and small-sample experiments support functional operation under the tested conditions and show that generated content still requires review. The system connects personal wrong-question study with continued practice. Probabilistic knowledge tracing has not been implemented, and long-term educational effectiveness requires further evaluation.
